about.heading: CAL SAILING TEAM
paragraphs: The California Golden Bears Sailing Team is a student-run, competitive racing team from the University of California at Berkeley. The team regularly competes in regattas throughout the San Francisco Bay and on the waters of Southern California and Hawaii.

The Cal Sailing Team was started in 1922 and is the second oldest club sport at Cal. Our fleet of fifteen FJs is located at Richmond Yacht Club, where we practice three days a week. Only thirty minutes from campus by car, Richmond Yacht Club is an incredible sailing facility with beautiful views of the Bay Area.
We are continually looking to expand our team’s skills and continue the Corinthian spirit at Cal.

articles.heading: Cascadia Cup, October 2025 — Washington
articles.excerpt: As the rest of the team was heading down to San Diego for Frosh-Soph and UCSD Open earlier this month, four of us flew up to Washington for the Cascadia Cup women's regatta...
paragraphs: As the rest of the team was heading down to San Diego for Frosh-Soph and UCSD Open earlier this month, four of us flew up to Washington for the Cascadia Cup women's regatta. When we touched down Friday evening, we were greeted with cold, rainy conditions.
Despite the weather, the team put in strong performances throughout the weekend and gained valuable fleet-racing experience against top women's teams from the region.

articles.heading: Frosh-Soph x UCSD Open, October 2025 — San Diego, CA
articles.excerpt: Over the weekend of October 11th and 12th, twenty of our beloved Cal sailors headed down to San Diego for the UCSD Open and Frosh Soph...
paragraphs: Over the weekend of October 11th and 12th, twenty of our beloved Cal sailors headed down to San Diego for the UCSD Open and Frosh Soph. It was many sailors' first time in San Diego — and for some, a first regatta.
The team brought energy and focus to Mission Bay, building skills in fleet racing and team logistics across two busy days on the water.

articles.heading: Cal Hosts Spring PCCs 2025 — Richmond, CA
articles.excerpt: We are excited to share that the Cal Sailing Team has been selected to host the Spring 2025 PCCSC Carter Ford Open Fleet race Championships!
articles.imageAlt: Spring PCCs 2025 at Richmond Yacht Club
paragraphs: We are excited to share that the Cal Sailing Team has been selected to host the Spring 2025 PCCSC Carter Ford Open Fleet race Championships!
Hosting at Richmond Yacht Club is a tremendous opportunity for our team to welcome conference rivals to the Bay and showcase the program our sailors build every week at practice.

articles.heading: Stoney Burke 2024 — Richmond, CA
articles.excerpt: Last weekend, the Cal Sailing Team was thrilled to host our home regatta, Stoney Burke, at Safe Harbor Marina Bay Yacht Club...
paragraphs: Last weekend, the Cal Sailing Team was thrilled to host our home regatta, Stoney Burke, at Safe Harbor Marina Bay Yacht Club, just south of Richmond Yacht Club.
Teams from across the conference joined us for a full weekend of racing. Thank you to everyone who volunteered, coached, and cheered on the Bears.

articles.heading: Hewitt Trophy Coed Interconference 2024 — Brunswick, ME
articles.excerpt: The Cal Sailing Team started the year off with a bang by jumping on a plane and heading for the East Coast...
paragraphs: The Cal Sailing Team started the year off with a bang by jumping on a plane and heading for the East Coast. Breaking away from the norm, we took on the challenges of an interconference regatta right off the bat.
Racing in new conditions against unfamiliar fleets pushed our sailors to adapt quickly and compete at a high level away from home waters.

articles.heading: Frosh Soph 2024 — San Diego, CA
articles.excerpt: Frosh Soph 2024 was yet another beautiful weekend in San Diego hosted by UCSD at Mission Bay Yacht Club...
paragraphs: Frosh Soph 2024 was yet another beautiful weekend in San Diego hosted by UCSD at Mission Bay Yacht Club. The classic mix of competitive and new sailors were more on fire than ever before.
Chaotic moments on and off the water always ended with great team energy, and our frosh and sophomores left with stronger boathandling and race IQ.

articles.heading: Top 9 Invitational / Women PCCs 2024 — Stanford, CA
articles.excerpt: On October 26 and 27, Cal Sailing made the 45 minute drive down to Redwood City to compete at the Top 9 Invitational and Women's PCCs hosted by Stanford...
paragraphs: On October 26 and 27, Cal Sailing made the short drive to Redwood City to compete at the Top 9 Invitational and Women's PCCs hosted by Stanford.
The format differed from most college sailing regattas, with only the top teams invited — a great test for our women's squad against the best in the conference.

articles.heading: Big Sail 2024 — Saint Francis Yacht Club
articles.excerpt: The team competed against Stanford in the annual Big Sail...
paragraphs: The team competed against Stanford in the annual Big Sail at Saint Francis Yacht Club.
Big Sail is one of the highlights of our rivalry season, bringing alumni, supporters, and current sailors together for match racing on the Bay.

articles.heading: Gala 2024 — Fort Mason in SF
articles.excerpt: The team raised money through a live auction at our annual Cal Sailing gala...
paragraphs: The team raised money through a live auction at our annual Cal Sailing gala in Fort Mason.
Thank you to everyone who attended, donated, and helped make the evening a success for our sailors and our program.

articles.heading: Rainbow Invite 2024 — Honolulu, Hawaii
articles.excerpt: Over winter break, team members had a taste of Hawaii as they competed at the Rainbow Invite...
paragraphs: Over winter break, team members had a taste of Hawaii as they competed at the Rainbow Invite.
Warm water and tradewind sailing made for an unforgettable regatta and a great way to cap the calendar year.

sections.heading: About Us
paragraphs: The Cal Sailing Team competes in the PCCSC (Pacific Coast College Sailing Conference), which sanctions collegiate racing on the Pacific Coast and is part of the larger ICSA (Intercollegiate Sailing Association). Cal races against schools such as Stanford, USC, University of Hawaii, UC Santa Barbara, and California Maritime Academy. The team is entirely student-run. We sail FJs at Richmond Yacht Club in the San Francisco Bay. Each year, we host our annual Stoney Burke regatta.

Practices are held Tuesday, Wednesday, and Friday afternoons at Richmond Yacht Club and go from 3pm until dark. Each practice generally follows the practice plan outlined below. The team holds weekly meetings on Mondays at 7pm to discuss team logistics and updates. The team uses Slack as a main form of communication.
Cal Sailing is open to any UC Berkeley students interested in competitive collegiate sailing. To get involved, email us at calsailing@gmail.com.

sections.heading: Recruitment & Joining the Team
paragraphs: We are a competitive racing team, and members are expected to start competing almost immediately. People without prior experience may still join if they can attend at least two practices a week and are dedicated to learning racing. Absolute beginners can start with Cal Adventures or the Cal Sailing Club for introductory lessons.
Prospective members should reach out to the recruitment chair and email calsailing@gmail.com.

sections.heading: FAQ
bullets: Competitions are open to undergraduates. Graduate students may practice with the team if they are not competition-eligible.
Dues are $310 per semester, covering travel, fleet maintenance, and a $55 collegiate membership to Richmond Yacht Club. Talk to the team if cost is a barrier — we are flexible.

High school students interested in sailing for Cal should contact calsailing@gmail.com during fall of senior year. We recommend visiting campus and practicing with the team in September or October before applying to Berkeley.
